title: Flat cycle sheaves of an acyclic K-flat complex
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Let $A^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] which is acyclic [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules], K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], and has flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For every integer $n$, the cycle sheaf $Z^n(A^\bullet)=\ker(d^n:A^n\to A^{n+1})$ is flat over $\mathcal O$.

proof.text: Fix an integer $n$ and a sheaf $N$ of $\mathcal O$-modules. Apply [lem-pur-acyclic-kflat-tensor-arbitrary] to the acyclic K-flat complex $A^\bullet$ and the complex $N[0]$ concentrated in degree zero. It gives acyclicity of $\operatorname{Tot}(N[0]\otimes_{\mathcal O}A^\bullet)$. In degree $i$ the only nonzero summand is $N\otimes_{\mathcal O}A^i$ and the differential is $1_N\otimes d^i$, because the first differential is zero and $(-1)^0=1$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Thus this ordinary tensor complex is exact in degree $n-2$ [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules].

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-opcycles-tor-criterion] with $P^\bullet=A^\bullet$ and index $n-1$. The terms are flat by hypothesis, and Step 1 gives exactness after tensoring with every $N$ in degree $(n-1)-1=n-2$. Hence $Q^{n-1}=A^{n-1}/\operatorname{im}(d^{n-2})$ is flat.

proof.text: Acyclicity gives $\ker(d^{n-1})=\operatorname{im}(d^{n-2})$ and $\operatorname{im}(d^{n-1})=\ker(d^n)$ [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules]. The map $d^{n-1}$ therefore induces an isomorphism $Q^{n-1}\cong Z^n(A^\bullet)$. For each sheaf $N$, tensoring this isomorphism gives a natural isomorphism $N\otimes Q^{n-1}\cong N\otimes Z^n(A^\bullet)$; the exact tensor functor for $Q^{n-1}$ consequently identifies with the tensor functor for $Z^n(A^\bullet)$, proving its flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].
